summary.type_ja: 型A：背景 → 利点 → 欠点
paras: Japan has long been known as a country where people prefer to pay in cash. Even after credit cards became widespread, many shoppers continued to carry cash and felt uneasy about spending money they could not see. In recent years, however, this habit has begun to change. Smartphone payment apps and contactless cards have proliferated, and the government has encouraged their use by offering points and other rewards to consumers.

Proponents of cashless payments point out several benefits. Customers can pay quickly without searching for coins, and they can easily check their spending records on their phones. Businesses also gain, because they spend less time counting cash at the end of the day or taking it to the bank. In addition, some experts believe that electronic records make it harder for people to hide their income in order to avoid paying taxes.

Nevertheless, not everyone is ready to give up cash. Many elderly people find payment apps confusing, and some small shops are reluctant to accept cashless payments because they must pay fees to payment companies. There are also concerns about security, as personal information could be stolen by criminals. Furthermore, power outages during natural disasters can make electronic payments impossible, which is one reason why many people still keep some cash at home.
summary.model: Although Japanese people have traditionally preferred cash, cashless payment methods have recently become popular, partly thanks to government incentives. They let customers pay faster and track their spending, save businesses time handling cash, and may curb tax evasion. However, older people often find them difficult, small stores dislike the fees, personal data may be stolen, and blackouts caused by disasters can make such payments impossible.

essay.topic: Agree or disagree: Students should be allowed to use AI tools when doing their homework
paras: I disagree with the idea that students should be allowed to use AI tools when doing their homework. I have two reasons for this opinion.

First, relying on AI would prevent students from truly learning. Homework is meant to train students to think through problems independently. If an AI tool writes their essays or solves their math problems, they may submit excellent work without understanding the content, and their skills might even deteriorate.

Second, allowing AI would undermine fairness in grading. Students who have access to advanced AI services could easily earn top marks, while those who do not might receive lower grades despite their efforts. Moreover, teachers would find it almost impossible to determine how much of the work each student actually did.
For these reasons, I believe that students should not be permitted to use AI tools for their homework.

expressions.en: I disagree with the idea that
expressions.ja: 〜という考えに反対だ（TOPIC の文をそのまま続けられる）
prevent A from doing：A が〜するのを妨げる
be meant to do：〜するためのものだ
find it … to do：〜するのは…だと分かる（形式目的語の it）
悪化する・衰える（準1級の重要語）
undermine：〜を（徐々に）損なう。評価の公平性を損なう

essay.note_ja: Learning は「AI が家庭教師になる」なら賛成、「自分で考えなくなる」なら反対の理由になる。POINTS はどちらの立場にも使えるものが多いので、POINTS を見て「説明と具体例がすぐ浮かぶ側」を選ぶと速い。Agree or disagree 型の TOPIC は、I agree that / I disagree with the idea that のあとに TOPIC の文を続けて書き出すと、立場がはっきりする。

opposite.stance_en: I agree that students should be allowed to use AI tools when doing their homework.

reasons.topic_en: First, learning to use AI tools well is good preparation for students' future careers.
reasons.support_ja: 多くの職場ですでに AI が使われている。学生のうちに、AI の答えをうのみにせず確かめながら使う力をつけておくべきだ。

reasons.topic_en: Second, AI tools can help students learn more effectively.
reasons.support_ja: わからない問題があっても、AI がその場で一人ひとりに合わせて説明してくれる。塾や家庭教師に頼れない生徒にとっては、学習の差を縮める助けにもなる。
